rules.all: giveaway_risk>=7, one_sided>=7, familiarity<6, kind_of, is_set, not same_kind, unsafe, misfiled, tier_guess two tiers off

pairs.note: Both are frozen creamy treats sold at carts; the telling difference is dense kulfi on a stick or in a matka versus machine-swirled softy in a cone.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Dense and slow-frozen, comes on a stick or in a matka
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Squeezed from a machine in a swirl into a cone
evidence.shared_clue: Cold, creamy and sold at roadside stalls

pairs.note: Both are bakery rolls with cream and the names get mixed up; the key difference is a sponge cake rolled round jam/cream versus a flaky pastry horn or roll filled with cream.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Soft sponge cake sliced into spiral rounds
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Flaky layered pastry shell stuffed with cream
evidence.shared_clue: Sweet, creamy and bought from a bakery

pairs.note: Loosely related desserts; the first clue (crunchy and baked vs cold and melting) exposes the imposter.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Baked and crunchy, goes well dunked in milk
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Melts if you leave it out, served in a scoop
evidence.shared_clue: Sweet and kids love it

pairs.note: Both are East-Asian-style stuffed snacks; distinguishing rests on steamed dough pockets versus fried rolled wrappers, though fried dumplings blur it.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Steamed pockets of dough, often served in a basket
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Crispy rolled wrapper fried until golden
evidence.shared_clue: Filled with vegetables and eaten with a chilli sauce

pairs.note: Different snacks; popcorn is the obvious cinema snack while pretzel is less familiar in India, which may hurt the Pretzel holder.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Eaten at the cinema from a big tub
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Twisted into a knot shape and sprinkled with salt
evidence.shared_clue: Salty crunchy snack

pairs.note: Similar social insects with colonies; termites eat wood and build mounds ('white ants'), ants are the generic ones, so clues overlap heavily.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Marches in a line to carry crumbs and sugar
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Eats wooden furniture and doors
evidence.shared_clue: Lives in a large colony with a queen

pairs.note: Both are counter-service government-style places for forms and money; stamps, letters and parcels vs loans and ATM separate them.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: You go there for a loan or an ATM
evidence.clue_B_not_A: You go there to send a letter or a parcel
evidence.shared_clue: Queue at a counter and fill a form

pairs.note: Both house large vehicles, but sirens and emergencies versus routes and passengers expose the imposter at the first clue.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Siren blares and crew rushes out in an emergency
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Conductors and drivers start routes with passengers
evidence.shared_clue: Big vehicles parked in rows

pairs.note: Both are casual food stops; dhaba is a fixed highway eatery with charpai seating while a food truck is a vehicle that moves.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Highway stop with charpai seating and truckers
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Drives to a new spot and serves from a window
evidence.shared_clue: Cheap, casual food eaten outdoors

pairs.note: Two very different Indian states; backwaters and coconut vs deserts and forts give many easy clues.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Backwaters, houseboats and coconut trees
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Desert, camels and old forts and palaces
evidence.shared_clue: Popular domestic holiday state

pairs.note: Both are Asian countries but quite different; Himalayan kingdom and monasteries vs beaches, motorbikes and pho.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Mountain kingdom with monasteries and no need for a visa for Indians
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Coastline, motorbikes and pho noodles
evidence.shared_clue: Asian country with lovely scenery

pairs.note: Both work in a school and clues overlap strongly; the difference is teaching a class versus running the school and disciplining students.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Teaches a subject and checks homework in a class
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Runs the whole school and gives suspensions
evidence.shared_clue: Students are scared of them at school

pairs.note: Both talk to an audience for a living; screen and serious news vs radio and music banter.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Reads headlines on camera in a studio
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Plays songs and jokes on radio with only a voice
evidence.shared_clue: Talks to a big audience every day

pairs.note: Both are music performers; singing live with their own voice versus mixing tracks on decks.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Sings with their own voice and a microphone
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Mixes songs on a console with headphones
evidence.shared_clue: Performs at weddings and parties

pairs.note: Both are friend-group party games of questions; dares and physical tasks versus choosing between two options.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Someone gets challenged to do a silly task
evidence.clue_B_not_A: You choose between two odd options
evidence.shared_clue: Played in a circle at a sleepover or party

pairs.note: Both are old bearded wizard mentors; Middle-earth, staff and Hobbits vs Hogwarts, wand and Harry.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Carries a staff and travels with Hobbits
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Heads a school and teaches Harry
evidence.shared_clue: Old wise wizard with a long white beard

pairs.note: Both are famous leaders with deep voices, but a dark masked Sith vs a truck-transforming robot hero separate them quickly.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Wears a black mask and breathes heavily
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Transforms into a truck
evidence.shared_clue: Has a deep booming voice and leads others

pairs.note: Both are Cartoon Network characters; alien watch transformations vs a blond pompadour trying to impress women.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Uses a watch to turn into aliens
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Has big blond hair and sunglasses
evidence.shared_clue: Cartoon on kids TV

pairs.note: Both are clever Indian storybook/comic figures; Chacha Chaudhary has a red turban and Sabu with a brain faster than a computer, Tenali Raman is a court jester in Vijayanagara.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Has a red turban and Sabu the giant
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Witty courtier who advises a king with funny stories
evidence.shared_clue: Clever Indian character known for brains

pairs.note: Both are swaggering Bollywood cops; Singham is Ajay Devgn's serious Maharashtra cop, Chulbul Pandey is Salman's quirky UP cop with collar-up sunglasses.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Famous roar, Goa and Maharashtra setting
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Sunglasses hooked on the collar, Uttar Pradesh
evidence.shared_clue: Police uniform and tough fights

pairs.note: Near-identical music streaming apps; most clues fit both. Distinguishing clues exist but are subtle (green logo and Wrapped vs Jio telecom tie-in and strong Bollywood/regional catalogue), and Spotify is the obvious global default.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Its year-end Wrapped recap gets shared everywhere
evidence.clue_B_not_A: It often comes bundled with a telecom recharge plan
evidence.shared_clue: I use it for playlists and offline downloads

pairs.note: Both are everyday Indian food brands with overlap (butter, cheese, packaged foods), but Amul is dairy-led (milk, the girl mascot) while Britannia is biscuit/bread-led (Good Day, Marie). A blank-mode imposter could guess either from a milk or biscuit clue.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: You'd find it in the dairy aisle with a cartoon girl on the hoardings
evidence.clue_B_not_A: It makes the biscuit you dunk in chai
evidence.shared_clue: You'll find it in every kirana shop

pairs.note: Both are beeping detectors; metal detectors are at security gates and treasure hunts, smoke detectors are on ceilings.

evidence.clue_A_not_B: Walk through it at an airport or mall entrance
evidence.clue_B_not_A: Fixed to the ceiling and beeps when kitchen burns
evidence.shared_clue: Beeps loudly to warn you

note: Final blind re-check of every Pair whose words changed in the v2 audit (23 Pairs). Three rounds: Spotify/Duolingo and Cred/Zepto failed round 1; Zepto/Rapido failed round 2; this file holds the last verdict per Pair.
